instruction:
For this task, start with an incomplete solid-mechanics template `/home/user/Desktop/elasticity_base.py`. Run your scripts with Python in the legacy FEniCS/DOLFIN 2019.1.0 environment (e.g. `from dolfin import *`). On this machine, run legacy FEniCS with `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/conda run --no-capture-output --prefix /home/user/miniconda3/envs/fenics-legacy python` when working on `elasticity_base.py`.

Complete the following: 1. Modify and generate `/home/user/Desktop/elasticity.py`: - Fully fix the left end face (`DirichletBC`, all displacement components) - Apply uniform traction `(0, -10, 0)` on the right end face (equivalent end load) - Define strain: `epsilon = 0.5*(grad(u) + grad(u).T)` - Define stress: `sigma = E/(1+nu)*[epsilon + nu/(1-2*nu)*tr(epsilon)*I]` - Solve 2. Run and extract: - Free-end point `(x, y, z) = (100, 10, 5)` UY displacement - Global maximum von Mises stress, projected cellwise to DG0 - Save to `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` in this format: `tip_uy, max_mises`
